Field notes 06 · 1 July 2026

They are just like that

The sentence that explains everything and examines nothing.

They are arrogant.
They are chaotic.
They do not know what they are doing.
They are making this difficult on purpose.

That is one end of a cross-border programme. At the other end, the list sounds different, and does the same work.

They are rigid.
They are entitled.
They wait for permission from above.

These sentences explain everything and examine nothing. That is why they are so useful, and why they become so expensive.

Once the other side becomes the explanation, there is nothing left to look at. Not the decision everyone avoided. Not the constraint people worked around. Not the signal that softened on the way up. Not the work quietly redone to keep the programme looking alive.

The cost does not show up immediately as one number. It shows up as effort. Overtime. Rework. Meetings that repeat the same ground with different frustration. Nothing gets fixed. It only moves.

No one reaching for this story is stupid or cruel. When a failure lands in your hands, the system offers a version you can survive. The story is always there. That is what makes it hard to refuse.

I have watched teams do the harder work. They looked at the system underneath the verdict. Patiently. Without superiority. They found constraints that had been treated as attitude, and signals that meant one thing at one end and something else at the other.

And I have watched someone in the same room reach past all of it for the older sentence. They are just like that. Understanding was on the table. The story was easier.

The real work sits one level under that verdict. Make the system visible enough, and the other side stops being the only explanation in the room. That is where my work starts.

Anna Chodynicka, DRIFT Partners · First published on LinkedIn, 1 July 2026
